blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In practice, most companies run a mix of on-premise and cloud, and the intermediate skill is knowing what belongs where. Highly sensitive data, systems with strict regulatory requirements, or workloads where latency is critical may still belong on-premise. Everything else — email, file sharing, analytics, development environments, customer-facing apps — usually sits better in the cloud.

What matters is consistency. A company that moves things between on-premise and cloud without clear rules ends up with inventory problems, security gaps, and duplicated work. A simple rule set — 'sensitive data here, everything else there' — is usually enough to keep the environment clean for years.

The goal is never to be 'fully cloud' or 'fully on-premise'. It is to be deliberate about which system lives where, and why.

items.q: According to the text, what is the intermediate skill in running a mixed environment?
options: Moving everything to the cloud as fast as possible
items.why: "the intermediate skill is knowing what belongs where" — decidir onde cada sistema deve viver.

items.q: Which type of workload may still belong on-premise?
items.why: "systems with strict regulatory requirements… may still belong on-premise."

items.q: What happens to a company that moves things without clear rules?
options: It ends up with inventory problems, security gaps, and duplicated work
items.why: "ends up with inventory problems, security gaps, and duplicated work."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A hybrid environment can stay clean for years with a simple rule set
Some sensitive data is better kept on-premise
Consistency matters more than the label of the setup
Being 'fully cloud' should be the ultimate goal for every company
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente que a meta nunca é ser 'fully cloud' ou 'fully on-premise'.

items.q: The phrase 'sensitive data here, everything else there' suggests that…
options: cloud should never hold company data
the rules must be long and highly technical to work
a clear, simple rule can be more effective than a complex one
items.why: Inferência: o autor apresenta uma regra curta como suficiente para manter o ambiente organizado por anos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry explicando o conjunto de regras que ele está escrevendo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, I finally sat down and wrote the one-page rule set. Honestly, I think everyone knew we needed it, but nobody wanted to be the person to write it down.

The rule itself is short. Sensitive data — trading systems, anything with a regulatory requirement, anything where latency really matters — stays on-premise. Everything else goes to the cloud: email, file sharing, analytics, the development environments. If it isn't sensitive and it doesn't need to be milliseconds fast, it belongs in the cloud.

What I'm really trying to fix is the drift. For years we moved workloads back and forth with no clear reason, and we ended up with security gaps and duplicated work. Two teams were paying for the same thing without knowing it. That's the kind of mess a simple rule prevents.

I'm not asking anyone to migrate everything overnight. We'll move things gradually, one workload at a time. The point isn't to be fully cloud or fully on-premise — it's to be deliberate. Every system should live somewhere for a reason we can actually explain.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Harry say nobody had written the rule set before?
options: Because the company banned written rules
Because the cloud provider forbade it
Because nobody wanted to be the person to write it down
items.why: "everyone knew we needed it, but nobody wanted to be the person to write it down."

items.q: According to Harry, what stays on-premise?
options: Sensitive data, regulatory systems, and latency-critical work
items.why: "Sensitive data… anything with a regulatory requirement… where latency really matters — stays on-premise."

items.q: What problem is Harry really trying to fix?
options: The cost of the cloud provider
The drift of moving workloads back and forth with no clear reason
The speed of the trading systems
items.why: "What I'm really trying to fix is the drift."

items.q: What does the example of two teams paying for the same thing illustrate?
options: That the cloud is always more expensive
That duplicated work and hidden waste come from having no clear rule
items.why: Inferência: ele cita o pagamento duplicado como exemplo da 'bagunça' que uma regra simples evita.

items.q: What is Harry's overall attitude toward the migration?
options: Rushed — he wants everything moved overnight
Indifferent — he leaves the choice to each team
Reluctant — he opposes using the cloud at all
Measured — deliberate and gradual, one workload at a time
items.why: Inferência: ele rejeita a migração de tudo de uma vez e defende ser 'deliberate' e gradual.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We run a mixed environment, with some systems local and others in the cloud." A mixed environment is…
options: a system that only uses the cloud
a network with no security rules
an office with people from different countries
a setup that combines on-premise and cloud systems
items.why: Mixed environment = ambiente misto: parte on-premise, parte na nuvem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The audit failed because a ___ let outsiders reach the internal files."
items.why: Security gap = lacuna de segurança, a falha que expôs os arquivos.

items.q: "Trading data can't wait, so critical latency keeps it on-premise." Critical latency refers to…
options: a situation where even tiny delays are unacceptable
the total cost of the servers
items.why: Critical latency = latência crítica: qualquer atraso, mesmo pequeno, é inaceitável.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Storing this data abroad breaks a ___, so it must stay in the country."
items.why: Regulatory requirement = exigência regulatória, uma norma legal a cumprir.

items.q: "We were deliberate about where each system lives." Being deliberate means…
options: acting slowly and without a plan
items.why: Deliberate = deliberado: uma escolha consciente e com razão clara.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de infraestrutura e TI. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Security still has to sign off on the new rule set." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the cloud migration one workload at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two engineers pushed back on moving the trading system to the cloud." They…
options: resisted or disagreed with the idea
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the rules but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's not lock ourselves into a single provider we can't leave." To lock yourself into something means to…
options: commit in a way that is hard to reverse
items.why: Lock yourself into = se prender a algo difícil de reverter (ex.: vendor lock-in).
